==Characteristics==
==={{OoT|-}}===
{{Descriptions OoT}}
In {{OoT}}, Phantom Ganon is the [[Boss]] of the [[Forest Temple (Ocarina of Time)|Forest Temple]].<ref name="OoT Navi"/> Once the battle starts, Phantom Ganon jumps into one of the six paintings around the room. Afterwards, it and two replicas will ride to the front of three paintings. The real one can be spotted by its lighter color. A purple vortex then appears revealing the real Phantom Ganon.<ref name="OoT Navi 2"/> As Phantom Ganon jumps out of the painting, Link can shoot it with the [[Fairy Bow]]. If the [[Arrow]] misses or is delayed, it summons an electric ball on the ground that scatters across the platform. This can be avoided by standing on one of the [[Triforce]] images on each corner of the platform. After three shots, Phantom Ganon leaves its horse, starting the second part of the battle.

Phantom Ganon now attacks by shooting an energy ball from its staff at Link while hovering over the ground. Link can hit the ball back with the [[Master Sword]] or a [[Bottle]]. After enough hits, Phantom Ganon falls to the ground paralyzed, where it can be hit multiple times with the Master Sword. When its health is halved, Phantom Ganon can also attack by twirling his staff a few times and then charging at Link, dealing three [[heart]]s of damage. Once defeated, he is banished to the gap between dimensions by Ganondorf<ref name="OoT Ganondorf"/> and Link receives a [[Heart Container]] as well as the [[Forest Medallion]].

{{Descriptions TWW}}
In {{TWW}}, Phantom Ganon appears in the [[Forsaken Fortress]] and in [[Ganon's Castle]].<ref name="TWW Prima 33"/> It must be defeated by reflecting its blue orbs with the Sword or an empty [[Bottle]].<ref name="TWW Manual 79"/><ref name="TWW Prima 33"/> Once hit by a reflected attack, Link can attack Phantom Ganon with his Sword. He can also attack it by intercepting its Sword attacks. After defeating Phantom Ganon in the Forsaken Fortress, Link receives the [[Skull Hammer]].<ref name="TWW Prima 79"/>

During its fight in Ganon's Castle, Phantom Ganon is accompanied by four illusions of itself. It now also attacks by throwing dark energy balls, which splits into a group of small bursts of energy flying towards Link. These can be sent back at it with a [[Spin Attack]]. After just one hit, Phantom Ganon disappears, leaving its Sword behind with the handle pointing at the door Link must open to advance.<ref name="TWW Stone in Ganon's Tower"/> Once the [[Light Arrow]]s are found, they must be shot at Phantom Ganon once stunned in order to finally defeat it.

Link can grab Phantom Ganon's Sword to attack; however, it must be held with both hands, leaving Link unable to use his [[Shield]]. After defeating Phantom Ganon in Ganon's Castle's labyrinth, Link must throw its Sword at the brick wall to gain access to the top of the Tower.<ref name="TWW Prima 119"/>

==={{FSA|-}}===
In {{FSA}}, Phantom Ganon first appears as the boss of [[Hyrule Castle (Dungeon)|Hyrule Castle]]. In order to defeat it, the [[Links]] must hit its energy balls back and forth with the Sword. Once stunned, it is vulnerable to slashes from the Sword. Phantom Ganon appears once again as the boss of the [[Temple of Darkness]]; however, it now summons clones to its aid. The real Phantom Ganon will throw green orbs that can be hit back, while the clones  throw white balls that break when hit with the Sword.

In {{BotW}}, [[Windblight Ganon]], [[Thunderblight Ganon]], [[Fireblight Ganon]], and [[Waterblight Ganon]] are all collectively known as Phantom Ganons.<ref name="CaC 80"/> They are [[Calamity Ganon]]'s creations that he sent out to the [[Divine Beast]]s, resulting in the death of the [[Champions]].<ref name="BotW Daruk"/><ref name="BotW Mipha"/><ref name="BotW Revali"/><ref name="BotW Urbosa"/> When Link tries to activate the Main Control Unit of a Divine Beast, these Phantom Ganons will appear, and they must be defeated in order to continue.<ref name="BotW Daruk 2"/><ref name="BotW Mipha 2"/><ref name="BotW Revali 2"/><ref name="BotW Urbosa 2"/> When Link is victorious, a [[Heart Container]] will drop, and he will have access to the Main Control Unit.

Link can also dress up as the Phantom himself with the [[Phantom Ganon Set]] after completing the "[[EX Treasure: Dark Armor]]" [[Side Quest]], which is exclusive to {{TMT}} [[Downloadable Content]] Pack. The Phantom Ganon Set is comprised of the [[Phantom Ganon Skull]], [[Phantom Ganon Armor]], and [[Phantom Ganon Greaves]]. It is rumored that some believe this [[Armor Set]] is possessed by a dark entity resembling the [[Ganondorf|Great King of Evil himself]].<ref name="CaC 191"/><ref name="BotW Inventory"/><ref name="BotW Inventory 2"/><ref name="BotW Inventory 3"/> Each piece of the set grants [[Stealth Up]] and has the same set bonus as the [[Radiant Set]], increasing the attack power of the [[Bokoblin Arm]], [[Moblin Arm]], and [[Lizalfos Arm]] bone [[Weapon]]s. The Phantom Ganon Set also disguises Link from all Stal enemies, save for [[Stalnox]] and [[Curse]]d Enemies.

{{Stub|TotK}}
[[Ganondorf]] utilizes Phantom Ganons disguised as [[Zelda]] to sow confusion across [[Hyrule]]. Two waves of Phantom Ganons (a set of three followed by a set of five) are fought inside the [[Sanctum]] at [[Hyrule Castle (Dungeon)|Hyrule Castle]] during the Main Quest as a Boss. A Phantom Ganon also appears when entering the insides of the [[Great Deku Tree]] in the [[Korok Forest]]. If a [[Gloom Spawn]] is defeated, a Phantom Ganon will appear where the last arm is slain immediately afterwards. In the distant past, Ganondorf used a Phantom Ganon disguised as Zelda to distract [[Sonia|Queen Sonia]] so that he could sneak up on her and kill her.

Phantom Ganons can be equipped with a [[Gloom Sword]], [[Gloom Club]], or [[Gloom Spear]], as well as a [[Demon King's Bow]]. While wielding a Gloom Club, they are capable of kicking Link. In between attacks, they will jump backwards and kick at Link if he is close to them. At low health, they will begin spreading Gloom around them to drain Link's maximum health and reduce his room to maneuver. When defeated, they will drop their Weapons and [[Dark Clump]]s. If they spot Link in a location they cannot reach, they will equip Demon King's Bows to attack from a distance. Attacks from a Phantom Ganon's melee Weapon or the Demon King's Bow will destroy any [[Zonai Device]]s they come into contact with.

The Phantom Ganons that appear from the Gloom Spawn are different from those at Hyrule Castle:
* Only one Phantom Ganon appears when a Gloom Spawn is defeated.
* If a Phantom Ganon loses sight of Link for a certain amount of time, it will perform a gloom spread attack.
* They cannot hear Link's noises (dashing, whistling, swinging a melee weapon, etc.). The same applies to the Gloom spawn.
* They can be defeated by Cuccos, while the last Phantom Ganon in each group in the Hyrule Castle battle can only be defeated by Link.

==Other Appearances==
==={{OoT|-}} (Himekawa)===
{{Noncanon|Start}}
Phantom Ganon appears in the {{OoT (Himekawa)}} first appearing in Chapter 2: "The Sage of the Forest: Saria", answering Ganondorf's call to guard the Forest Temple and strike down the Hero of Time. When Link and [[Mido]] walk by a painting of Ganondorf, Phantom Ganon attacks. Despite a good fight, Phantom Ganon is defeated when Mido throws Link the Bow, defeating the specter of the King of Evil and releasing [[Saria]] from the painting.

==={{HWL|-}}===
{{Noncanon|Start}}
{{Stub|HWL}}
In {{HWL}}, Phantom Ganon appears as a Giant Boss, and as the main villain of the [[Legend Mode#Wind Waker|Wind Waker]] series of Scenarios in [[Legend Mode]]. He had stolen [[Cia]]'s dark magic and the Triforce of Power from [[Lana]], creating a new dimensional rift that summons the world from the Era of the Great Sea. He is eventually defeated by Link, Lana, [[Tetra]], [[King Daphnes]], and Cia.

In battle, Phantom Ganon wields his sword, which he uses for various spin attacks. He is able to vanish and reappear closer to enemy Warriors for a surprise spin attack, or alternately to create copies of himself to surround and attack the Warrior. His projectile attacks consist of raising both of his arms to create many homing energy balls, or to simply create a single white energy ball. The latter can be used to expose his [[Weak Point Gauge]] if bounced back at him by striking it. Phantom Ganon has no specific weakness to any item, and the only way to damage him is by reflecting his own attacks at him.

After his health has been reduced to about half, he summons a second sword and switches his battle style to melee, using the two blades to violently hack at the enemy Warrior. He also lowers his hovering altitude, making himself reachable to attack, but will always shield himself similarly to {{TWW|-}} Ganondorf if attacked at the front or the sides. His backside, however, will become vulnerable to attack. After striking his back enough times, he will fall to the ground, exposing his Weak Point Gauge.

When defeated, Phantom Ganon will occasionally drop his [[Phantom Ganon's Cape|Cape]] as a silver [[Material]], and rarely, his [[Material|Sword]] as a gold Material.
{{Noncanon|End}}

[[Ganondorf]] makes use of Phantom Ganons to infiltrate both [[Hyrule Castle (Great Plateau)|Hyrule Castle]] and [[Mineru]]'s research stations in the [[Depths]]. One Phantom Ganon finds the [[Forbidden Construct]] beneath [[Tobio's Hollow]] and imbues it with [[Gloom]]. However, the Construct quickly absorbs the entire essence of the Phantom Ganon within itself as it awakens, destroying the Phantom Ganon double. Not particularly perturbed by this unexpected development, Ganondorf then used [[Monster Part]]s to create a second Phantom Ganon, which he successfully used in his plan to assassinate Queen [[Sonia]].

After becoming the [[Demon King Ganondorf|Demon King]], Ganondorf makes Phantom Ganon copies of his Demon King form to fight for him in the Depths. The first encounter against these new Phantom Ganons occurs during the [[Scenario]] "[[Purging the Shadows]]". Later, the [[Warrior]]s encounter more Phantom Ganons during "[[The Demon King, Ensnared]]".

Following the release of the {{Version|AoI|1.0.3|link}} update, after completing the main story, additional Phantom Ganons can be met as part of the [[Phantom Ganon Appearance]] mechanic.

Before becoming the Demon King, the Phantom Ganons resemble Ganondorf's future shriveled form, while the Phantom Ganons he creates with his [[Secret Stone of Darkness]] instead resemble his Demon King form.

==Trivia==
*In {{TWW|-}}, the [[Hylian Language|Hylian script]] on Phantom Ganon's Sword reads "[[Zubora]] [[Gabora]]", the names of the blacksmiths who forge Link's [[Kokiri Sword]] in {{MM}}.
*The [[Wall Merging]] ability from {{ALBW}} was inspired by Phantom Ganon from {{OoT|-}}, who also has the ability to enter walls through paintings.<ref name="E 302"/>
**In addition, his capturing of Saria in a painting would later be the main power of [[Yuga]], Ganon's Lorulean counterpart.
*Although Phantom Ganon himself does not appear, a concept art for Ganondorf in the ''Oracle'' games is described as representing "Ganondorf's phantom."<ref name="HH 169"/>
*Prior to {{Version|TotK|1.1.2|link}} of {{TotK}}, if Link shoots two consecutive [[Arrow]]s at Phantom Ganon's head between its attacks whilst he is not airborne, the second Arrow will not deal damage. The block or temporary invincibility is indicated by blue sparks. This was fixed by {{Version|TotK|1.1.2}} or prior, where it will always take damage from head shots.{{Verify|TotK}}<!--From personal testing, this seems to have been patched on 1.1.2 or prior. Further testing on versions 1.1.0 and 1.1.1 are needed to confirm. Something similar does occur during the final fight with Ganondorf, where shooting an arrow at him can sometimes be blocked/swatted away. The original edit adding this piece of trivia claimed it was due to the reuse of code. However, this was previously pointed out as not trivia.-->
